scalars.scalar_value: This is a full-time, 2 years, postdoctoral appointment with the possibility of renewal based upon satisfactory job performance, continuing availability of funds and ongoing operational needs. You must have less than 3 years of paid postdoctoral experience. Salary for Postdoctoral positions depends on years of experience post-degree.
Experience with performance optimization of scientific software is desirable.
Demonstrated research experience in the development of quantum algorithms, preferably for quantum chemistry or materials science applications.

items.item_text: This position is subject to a background check. Any convictions will be evaluated to determine if they directly relate to the responsibilities and requirements of the position. Having a conviction history will not automatically disqualify an applicant from being considered for employment.
Lawrence Berkeley National Lab, 1 Cyclotron Road, Berkeley, CA. A REAL ID or other acceptable form of identification is required to access Berkeley Lab sites (for more information ).

items.item_text: This position is not eligible for relocation assistance.
Candidates must be eligible to work in the U.S. at the time of hire. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.
Ph.D. degree in Applied Mathematics, Computer Science, Computational Chemistry, Physics, or a relevant field.
Demonstrated research experience in the development of quantum algorithms, preferably for quantum chemistry or materials science applications.
Experience with performance optimization of scientific software is desirable.
Experience in compiling quantum algorithms and executing experiments on quantum hardware.
Develop efficient and scalable Krylov-inspired quantum subspace methods.
Design, compile, and optimize quantum circuits for execution on neutral atom-based QPUs.
Develop and evaluate partial quantum error correction and error mitigation techniques compatible with current and emerging quantum hardware.
Collaborate in a multidisciplinary research environment with mathematicians, computer scientists, physicists, and domain scientists.
Disseminate research findings through publications in peer-reviewed journals and presentations at leading conferences.
Strong background in numerical linear algebra, including matrix decompositions, iterative methods, approximation theory, and optimization.
Proficiency in scientific programming using MATLAB/Python/Qiskit and MPI/OpenMP/Cuda.
Demonstrated track record of scientific writing evidenced by first-author publications in peer-reviewed journals.
This position has an anticipated start date of October 1, 2026.

We’re here for the same mission, to bring science solutions to the world. Join our team and YOU will play a supporting role in our goal to address global challenges! Have a high level of impact and work for an organization associated with 17 Nobel Prizes!
Why join Berkeley Lab?
Excellent written and oral communication skills.
Knowledge of randomized numerical linear algebra and randomized algorithms.
